sentences.text: Now the small stuff, and one daytime shape.
A sailing vessel under seven meters shows sidelights and a sternlight if practicable.
If she doesn’t, she must have an electric torch or a lighted lantern ready, showing a white light, and show it in enough time to prevent collision.
So that single white light waving at you off the beach at dusk may be a little daysailer, telling you she’s there.
A vessel under oars may show the sailing lights.
If not, she needs that same white torch or lantern ready.
By day, a vessel under sail that’s also being propelled by her engine shows a cone, point down, forward where it can best be seen.
Because with her sails up she looks like a sailboat, but under the rules she’s a power-driven vessel.
The cone tells you the truth.
And the Inland difference: under the Inland rules, a vessel under twelve meters isn’t required to show that cone, but may.
